content.comment_body: Can you confirm if inputs I1 and I2 on the [product_name] controller only detect analog signals in the 0-10V range? My device has the article number [article_no]. When I connect 4-20 mA sensors, I don't get a signal, but 0-10V works.

Try searching for "4-20mA" in relevant conferences about [product_name], as there are many discussions on this topic. You can't directly connect a 4-20mA sensor to the base module, but you can convert its current to voltage with a 500 Ohm resistor if you understand Ohm's law. Regards, [user_name]

The [product_name] base module with article number [article_no] does not have analog inputs. Only base modules of the 8.2 series with these article numbers: [article_no], [article_no], [article_no], [article_no], have four analog 0-10V inputs onboard.

Unfortunately, I didn't check the article number—you actually have the AC/DC version of the base module, so it can't accept analog signals, including outputs from a pH electrode. We mainly use the DC-only version with relay outputs, which has four analog and four high-speed counter inputs and works well for our machines. Regards, [user_name]
With all [product_name] modules marked [article_no] that feature analog inputs, there's a print label on the upper left corner of their housing (see the attached image).
Thanks! I've realized suddenly that I actually have three different models of controllers—thought they were all the same at first.

Thanks! I'm not focusing on the pH electrode just yet. I'm currently assembling a cabinet with multiple sensors and pneumatic devices. The pH project is a dream I haven't attempted yet—maybe when I get a signal booster I'll try.

To use 0/4-20mA sensors, it's best to use the module that's designed for them: [product_name] ([article_no]). Since the [product_name] you mentioned first ([article_no]) lacks analog inputs, you'll need [product_name] for both 0..10V and 0/4-20mA signals. It uses addresses AI1 and AI2.

analysis.insight_summary: The user attempted to connect 4-20mA sensors to inputs I1 and I2 on a [product_name] controller with article number [article_no], but no analog signal was recognized. Other members clarified that this base module does not support analog inputs, and that compatibility depends on specific models and article numbers. Advice was given to use a dedicated analog input module ([product_name]) for 0/4-20mA and 0-10V signals. There is some confusion about compatible hardware and module input differences.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects the controller's I1 and I2 inputs to be capable of reading both voltage and current analog signals, such as those from 4-20mA sensors, and wants clear information about which modules can support a range of sensor types.
